cohort: 392,458 primiparous women in Denmark with a singleton delivery between 1995 and 2012 and no previous psychiatric history
finding: Pregnancy and obstetrical complications, such as hyperemesis gravidarum, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, and Cesarean section, were associated with an increased risk of postpartum depression (PPD) and acute stress reactions, but not postpartum psychosis (PP).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of both PPD (IRR 1.32, 95% CI 1.13-1.53) and postpartum acute stress reactions (IRR 1.36, 95% CI 1.20-1.55).
